title: Vietnamese Food in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has one of Europe's best Vietnamese food scenes**, home to around 40,000 people of Vietnamese background, and most visitors miss it entirely.
**It grew out of real Berlin history:** 1980s contract workers in the East (Lichtenberg, Marzahn) and South Vietnamese refugees in the West.
**Think in three worlds:** central classics in Mitte (Monsieur Vuong, District Mot), sit-down dinners on Kantstrasse in the west, and relaxed, veg-friendly spots in Kreuzberg.
**The Dong Xuan Center in Lichtenberg is the deep dive:** a Vietnamese wholesale market with cheap, authentic pho. Take tram M8 and bring cash.
**Order pho first** (the noodle soup), then try bun, banh mi, fresh summer rolls (goi cuon), and a strong iced coffee (ca phe sua da).
**Vietnamese kitchens are some of Berlin's most reliable vegan options**, built around tofu, herbs and rice.
